text:
IncidentBot: SEV2 alert — spike in 5xx and sustained high latency for /v1/generate across eu regions. Auto-mitigation triggered: smart-routing fallback enabled. Paging on-call: @jess (SRE).
Jess: picking up pager, looking now. Can someone drop the alert graph? :eyes:
ops-bot: metric snapshot: 5xx rate eu-west-1 9.8% (baseline 0.6%), p95 latency eu-west-1 1.2s (baseline 120ms), error surge started ~2078465220 (8m ago).
Jess: thanks. Marco, any recent change in routing or model variants?
Marco: I pushed a routing policy tweak earlier today to allow fallback to smaller-quantised variants under load — intended for cost-shedding. Didn't expect it to be used yet.
Aisha: hmm which variant exactly?
Marco: policy points fallback -> model: rdx-large-8q (quantized). It's marked compatible in the catalog but we hadn't fully tested it for the new attention kernel.
Kai: customer support reporting multiple customers seeing repeated 500s and retries. Some clients show many repeated attempts in logs.
Liam: summary from customer-facing telemetry: 24 orgs hit, biggest 3 saw 40-60% error rates for their API requests in last 5m.
Jess: root trace: runtime returns CODEC_ERROR from rdx-large-8q, triggers smart-routing to failover to eu-west-2, which then triggers more retries from clients -> region spinups -> additional failures. Looks like client-side retry + server-side fallback loop amplifying traffic.
Marco: confirmed from trace: initial request -> rdx-standard -> on error routing policy kicks -> rdx-large-8q chosen -> model fails (serialization mismatch) -> runtime returns 5xx -> smart-routing policy treats as region/variant failure and sends to alternate region -> clients on 500 retry -> traffic double/triple.
Aisha: so two amplification vectors: (1) wrong variant was selected (not actually compatible) (2) clients have aggressive retry with no jitter/circuit breaker.
Jess: immediate mitigation: disable automatic fallback to quantized variants and set routing to fail closed (return 429/503 instead of attempting failover). I'm going to flip the policy.
Jess: running command to patch policy:```
# disable auto-fallback to quantized variants
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --smart-fallback false --fallback-variants ""
```
ops-bot: acknowledged. policy update queued to control plane, rolling to edge nodes.
Marco: while that rolls, we can hotpatch the model catalog to mark rdx-large-8q incompatible for that architecture:```
redwoodctl models set-compat rdx-large-8q --arch x86-avx2 --compatible false
```
Kai: telling support to advise customers to backoff retries and enable exponential jitter. Posting canned message now.
Liam: running a temporary throttling rule to limit per-key retries at the gateway to reduce thundering herd:```
redwoodctl gateway ratelimit set --key-rate 20r/m --burst 50 --on-exceed 429
```
IncidentBot: Control plane patch accepted, change-id: cp-9421, rolling to 12 edge clusters (eta ~2m).
Jess: monitoring. Metrics already show 5xx trending down in eu-west-1 but eu-west-2 is still noisy — likely the fallback spike.
Marco: adding a short-term circuit-breaker in smart-router: return 503 for variants that pass a 5xx threshold within 60s. Pushing change.
Aisha: can we also push a redirect to pinned model for active customers so we avoid fallback entirely? We can add a per-api-key override to pin to rdx-standard.
Jess: good idea. Liam, can you coordinate pinning for the top-3 affected customers?
Liam: on it. Sending keys to Marco over DM.
Kai: support message posted to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated errors in EU regions; temporary mitigation applied. Please reduce client retries and enable jitter. We'll follow up within 30 minutes." :speech_balloon: 
Jess: ops-bot shows control-plane rollout complete. Edge nodes reflect policy change. Gateway throttle applied.
ops-bot: metric update: eu-west-1 5xx down to 2.1%, p95 latency 420ms; eu-west-2 5xx at 3.8% (coming down). Overall request volume reduced ~35% due to gateway throttles.
Marco: logs show rdx-large-8q still occasionally receiving traffic from long-lived connections; scheduling a restart of serving processes in eu-west-2 to clear in-memory routing table.
Jess: I'm handing off to Marco for mitigation and detailed RCA. I'll remain on the thread for coordination. Marco, you're owning postmortem. If anything changes, tag me.
Marco: taking over. Immediate action items: 1) confirm model catalog compatibility flags and add integration test; 2) add canary for smart-fallback so we don't route >5% traffic to untested variants; 3) update docs and SDK to recommend exponential backoff and jitter; 4) short-term: add circuit-breaker thresholds and per-key pinning. I'll open PRs and link here.
Aisha: adding an alert tuning ticket to prevent auto-fallback churn from generating new pages — we should debounce alert triggers for cascading failures.
Jess: customer impact note for status page: "We observed elevated error rates and latency for hosted API in EU regions due to an automated routing policy that routed traffic to an incompatible model variant. This caused repeated retries and region failover behavior, amplifying traffic (thundering herd). Immediate mitigations applied: disabled auto-fallback to quantized variants, applied gateway throttling, and pinned affected customers. Service is recovering; root cause investigation underway."
Liam: scheduled follow-up call in 30m to align on comms and postmortem owners.
Marco: creating postmortem draft now, will include timelines, config diffs, and tests. Tagging: @jess @aisha @kai.
Jess: thanks team — keep updates short here. I'll close the page when SLAs are green and affected customers confirm recovery. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Page closed by Jess at 2078465660.
